source.excerpt: Recollect that trifles make perfection, and that perfection is no trifle.
trail: Wikiquote places the longer “Recollect that trifles” wording under Disputed and cites Colton’s Lacon (1822) without an earlier citation. The fetched 1849 Lacon record also displays the anecdote among popular passages. This establishes a later literary attribution, not a Renaissance transcript. The attribution caveat ↗
Google Books identifies the 1849 edition and displays the sculptor anecdote in its popular passages. Lacon, 1849 edition ↗

author.heading: About Michelangelo
author.bio: Michelangelo was an Italian sculptor, painter, architect and poet. His later reputation made anecdotes about artistic patience attractive vehicles for advice, even when their documentary origins were unclear.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying is attached to a sculptor anecdote in a nineteenth-century quotation tradition. The story contrasts changes an observer overlooks with the artist’s attention to individual details, but its later publication does not establish an eyewitness report of Michelangelo.
